body:
# EngineShelf 1.1.8

## Fixed

- **The Windows manager stopped answering and the page never got past its
  loading skeleton.** No error, no log line, and it did not quit when the window
  was closed either. A browser opens more sockets than it sends requests on —
  the spare for a first answer that is slow, the one it preconnects for what it
  thinks is next — and reading from one that has not spoken yet waits until it
  does. On a manager that is a single thread, one silent socket meant nothing at
  all was answered: `/api/token` never came back, so nothing below it in the
  page ever ran. Sockets wait their turn now and are read from only once they
  have bytes for us. `server.py` serves on threads and was never affected.
- **EngineShelf would not open at all while Docker Desktop was starting up.**
  `docker info` against a daemon that is still coming up answers in its own
  time, and the manager asks before it opens its window — so nothing appeared,
  on a machine that may only have wanted the native launcher. Every question put
  to `docker` and `wsl` has an end to it now: eight seconds for a docker call,
  which is the limit `docker_out` has always had in `server.py`, and twenty for
  a `wsl` call that may have to boot the distro first. Measured against a
  `docker` and a `wsl` that never return at all, the window used to never open
  and now opens in sixteen seconds.
- **The system check could take the manager with it.** The same cause on the
  request path, where it froze a shelf somebody was using rather than one that
  had yet to draw. One state document also put the same questions to the machine
  twice over: five calls where three now do on a machine running Docker inside
  WSL, and `docker info` asked twice on one with Docker Desktop. On that machine
  that never replies, `/api/state` comes back in 16.3s instead of not at all;
  where Docker is healthy it answers in 0.46s, the same before and after.
- **A manager in trouble left the window with nothing to say.** The page had an
  answer for a request that failed and none for one that simply never came back:
  the error card, the retry and the log's own "the next one will do" are all
  written for a promise that settles. Every call gives up after twenty seconds
  now and draws the "Cannot reach the manager · Try again" card a stopped
  manager has always drawn. This half is `gui/app.js`, which both managers
  serve, so macOS and Linux have it too — what used to trigger it was Windows
  only.

Windows, apart from that last one. Every fix here is the Windows manager having
one thread where `server.py` has as many as it needs.

## Upgrading

- **Take this if you are on Windows.** In 1.1.7 the manager can stop answering
  before the shelf has drawn a single row, with nothing on screen to say that is
  what happened.
- Nothing else to do: extract over the old copy and start it. Browsers, profiles
  and containers are untouched.

Artifacts: `EngineShelf-1.1.8-macOS.zip`, `EngineShelf-1.1.8-Windows.zip`,
`EngineShelf-1.1.8-Linux.tar.gz`. Verify with `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
